items.title: Jensen Huang Reportedly Weighing Return as Nvidia CEO With Allies
items.excerpt: Jensen Huang has reportedly had discussions with his allies about a potential return as Nvidia's CEO just days after reports of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and multiple employees led to his resignation.
items.content_text: Jensen Huang has reportedly had discussions with his allies about a potential return as Nvidia's CEO just days after reports of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and multiple employees led to his resignation. Information on what is only the latest unexpected turn in a tangled web of updates for the tech giant came from a new Financial Times report. It stated that Huang has had private discussions with confidantes about the possibility of his reinstatement, as some Nvidia employees and minds from across Silicon Valley call for his return. Nvidia has found itself in headlines in the tech world for the wrong reasons the last week. The company's board announced it had launched an independent investigation into Huang just seven days ago as it looked into allegations that he had been unfaithful to his wife with an individual the U.S. government believed to be a spy working for the Chinese government. At the time, Nvidia said it "had no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised" but continued with the investigation to "examine all available information." It was a move that could rock any company, and it was just the start for Nvidia and Huang's week. The New York Times reported that the tech figurehead had an additional affair with company vice president of health care Kimberly Powell, who reported to him, just days later. Reuters launched its own report claiming he had another affair with a different employee that same day . Huang had announced his resignation as these reports emerged and as more rumors began to swirl, but the aftermath has only increased chatter online. Other giants in the tech space, including billionaire Elon Musk and Epic Games boss Tim Sweeney , have publicly called for his reinstatement. Now, Huang appears to be considering what that might look like himself. "Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen," one of Huang's allies, who also said Silicon Valley leaders were assembling a "war room" for his return with hopes to gain White House support, explained. The likelihood of the initiative panning out is unclear but is said to have Huang's support. However, if they continue their plan to get Huang back as Nvidia CEO, it won't be easy. He resigned from the company just days ago, and although the details of any alleged affairs remain unclear, there's no denying the damage done to his public reputation. One ally pushing for him to come back acknowledged that "having an affair with a subordinate is a fireable offense." Meanwhile, Nvidia is already actively working behind the scenes to find a replacement. Executive vice president and chief financial officer Colette Kress is currently serving as interim CEO in Huang's place. The Financial Times reported that the company's board had already approached Arm chief executive Rene Haas as a potential replacement. It's a rapidly developing and unprecedented situation with ramifications felt far outside the tech world. IGN examined what the changes might mean for GeForce going forward in the aftermath of Huang's resignation. Photo by Soeren Stache/picture alliance via Getty Images.

items.title: Xbox Confirms Project Helix Is 'a Console Capable of Playing Games From Your PC'
items.excerpt: Xbox has confirmed Project Helix is "designed to be a console capable of playing games from your PC."
items.content_text: Xbox has confirmed Project Helix is "designed to be a console capable of playing games from your PC." Microsoft unveiled a slew of details about its past, present, and future with the surprise publication of the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine . It's all part of surprise festivities meant to help celebrate 25 years of Xbox, and it also happens to have revealed more information about Project Helix than we've received in some time. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has called the next-gen project a "family of devices" before, and although that language is used again here, vice president of next generation Jason Ronald helped paint a clearer picture. The main idea here is that, through the ups and downs of Xbox's history, many lessons have been learned. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine – one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," Ronald said. "My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games." These are already big promises for Project Helix, which has been speculated to arrive as soon as late 2027, but what actually is it? There's no telling when we'll see what the family of devices it encompasses looks like, but today, Ronald was at least willing to sell Xbox fans on the idea of a project that seems to be centered more around the traditional idea of a console than anything else. "We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a Pc that can also play console games," he added. "The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it." Ronald said creating the next-gen project over the years hasn't just meant answering the questions of today, though; it's meant thinking ahead, too. Without directly addressing how it may pertain to the mysterious Xbox project, Ronald pointed to how Generation Alpha adapted to a world where content isn't locked to any one device. He also touched on how he believes the barriers to creation for things like user-generated gaming content "are going to come down" in the near future, saying players will eventually "have much more agency" and "control over their experiences." The Project Helix lead also recalled how Microsoft "lost sight of what is truly magical" with the Xbox One. Going forward, it's all about the players, developers, and the games that they love. No matter what Project Helix is, what it can do, or what games it plays, though, one thing is more important than almost anything else: price. The gaming industry is recoiling from a component crisis that has already considerably driven up the cost of enjoying the hobby. As prices for everything from consoles to storage skyrocket, the excitement that usually permeates the atmosphere of impending next-gen upgrades has been replaced by dread. Some players have even begun asking manufacturers like Sony and Microsoft to delay new hardware plans until prices come down – or at least until they can save enough money. It's brutal out there, but Ronald is optimistic when it comes to Project Helix. He even said that the current component crisis has driven the team to meet the challenge. "It's definitely a challenging time," he said, "but as a system and a platform designer, it's also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable. "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years." Microsoft believes Project Helix is a transition to the next generation of Xbox gaming consoles. To that point, Ronald said game preservation has been and will continue to be "core to Xbox." He and the team are already thinking ahead. "[Compatibility is] really informing how we design the platform and how we work with our partners to make sure that these games can not only be played, but they can also be played better than ever before in the future," he said. "Not only are we preserving those games from the past, but it's actually informing how we're designing and building the platform and games today – so that they can be preserved 20 years, 30 years in the future." Today's Xbox magazine piece also calls Project Helix the "crown jewel in a platform able to move with you." Ronald said the goal with the device is "removing barriers to play, removing friction, and those arbitrary boundaries that have existed in the past." "Our design goal is that no matter where you play," he explained, "it feels very intuitive and very distinctly 'Xbox,' but we also want to tailor it to the unique capabilities of the screen, whether that's a large-screen TV in your living room, whether you're playing on a console or you're streaming it to a small screen on a handheld device, or even on PC – where you have higher information density, you have a mouse and keyboard, you have more precision. We want it to feel very familiar, but also take advantage of the unique capabilities of the device you're actually playing on." Xbox pointed to the recently released ROG Xbox Ally and Xbox mode as a tease for the direction it's heading in. The feedback it's received on the front has already helped further pave the way for Project Helix, with Ronald going as far as to say that "we view the Ally as a precursor to what we're doing with Helix – but it's informed by a lot of the design concepts we have for Helix." As Xbox prepares Project Helix, it's winding down a busy and tumultuous year. Sharma taking charge in the first few months of 2026 signaled that a new chapter was about to unfold, but layoffs affecting thousands and shut-down game studios have made it hard for many to look forward to what's next. Sharma admitted Microsoft's gaming brand was "not healthy" in a July update . Sharma shared her vision for the next 25 years of gaming earlier this week. For more as Xbox turns 25, you can see how IGN helped celebrate the brand's big birthday. You can also check out the new nostalgic boot-up sequences added to consoles today.
items.title_en: Xbox Confirms Project Helix Is 'a Console Capable of Playing Games From Your PC'

items.title: Xbox Reveals Original and 360 Boot-Up Options for 25th Anniversary
items.excerpt: Microsoft has revealed three new nostalgic Xbox console boot-up options for Xbox Series X/S and Xbox One as part of a new update for the brand's 25th anniversary.
items.content_text: Microsoft has revealed three new nostalgic Xbox console boot-up options for Xbox Series X/S and Xbox One as part of a new update for the brand's 25th anniversary. Xbox has been around a long time, and those who have stuck around for the full ride have seen it through plenty of ups and downs. To mark the occasion, the company revealed all of the old-school animations that players can enjoy as soon as a new update rolls out for Series and One devices today. These three new animations are largely untouched rips of the same boot-up videos from some of the earliest days of Microsoft's gaming endeavors. The Original is the same sci-fi-inspired introduction that played for original Xbox consoles. The other two options are Xbox 360-themed, with one being based on the 2005 startup and the other based on the 2010 startup. We’re bringing back the original XBOX boot-up animation for all XBOX Series X|S and XBOX One players, along with two additional XBOX 360 boot-up animations! This update will be rolling out throughout the day and thank you for being part of 25 years of XBOX. https://t.co/V9SKMZTtPR — XBOX (@XBOX) November 15, 2026 Xbox has been going hard on the nostalgia to help celebrate its 25th anniversary today. In addition to the three new boot-up animations, Microsoft published the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine , which offered a full layout for the company's 25-year history in games and what's coming next. Part of the future includes plotting ahead for Project Helix , a project the company has previously described as a family of devices that could mark a new path forward for Xbox. It all arrives as Microsoft navigates a tough year for the brand, which has seen it introduce a new CEO in Asha Sharma and announce thousands of layoffs . Xbox is pushing ahead, but as for what 2027 will bring, we'll have to wait and see. IGN got in on the anniversary festivities with a trip down memory lane with Ryan McCaffrey . If you’ve yet to see the nostalgic Original and 360 boot-up animations on your Xbox Series X/S or One consoles, they should become available at some point later today. For more, you can check out the new sequence added earlier this year .

items.title: GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Will Start as Small-Time Criminals Who Have to Work Up to High-Value Jobs
items.excerpt: GTA 6 will let Jason and Lucia pull off high-value jobs, but Rockstar Games asks players to work up from being small-time criminals first.
items.content_text: GTA 6 will let Jason and Lucia pull off high-value jobs, but Rockstar Games asks players to work up from being small-time criminals first. The latest peek at this week's new Grand Theft Auto game arrived courtesy of a preview piece from The Guardian (via @GameRoll_ ). It included interviews with Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson and head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe, who covered the kind of people GTA 6 will cater to and the kind of people it's about. Jason and Lucia are two names we've heard for years, and they're not about to go away any time soon. After 13 years, faithful GTA fans will soon finally go hands-on with the next mainline game in the groundbreaking open-world sandbox series. They won't be able to immediately pull off front-page heists out of the gate, though. The Guardian said players won't be allowed to have the duo rob Vice City jewelry stores or drive around Leonida in sports cars in the early moments of GTA 6. Instead, they'll only be able to "hotwire low-end vehicles and pick basic locks" until they work their way up to high-value work later. What the threshold to reach those moments is remains unclear, but considering Rockstar has toiled away on the game for more than a decade, it's probably best that players don't burn their way to the top too quickly. Nelson described the "younger couple" as a pair with "their backs against the wall" when we first meet them. We've known that GTA 6 takes after Red Dead Redemption 2 in some respects, so Jason and Lucia won't be whipping out RPGs from their back pocket – at least at first. The piece added that robbing everything from gas stations to upscale mall boutiques might be easier or more fruitful if players take the time to complete extra steps. That might mean disabling security cameras or stealing surveillance footage, or it could mean scoping out locations for more discreet entry points. Skip the prep and a robbery might get chaotic quickly. That's where thinking on your toes will prove beneficial not only for your success but for Jason and Lucia, too. Judging by some of the Wanted System changes Rockstar has detailed in the past, players might want to think twice before making any knee-jerk reactions. A more detailed and realistic world line with another new element Rockstar accounted for: empathy . As detailed by The Guardian, Nelson and the rest of the team have promised that GTA 6 includes "mechanisms for encouraging" empathy for the first time in series history. What exactly that means remains to be seen, but with many details and different ways to play, we probably won't fully understand the developers' vision until we meet Jason and Lucia ourselves. GTA 6 launches for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19. For more, you can check out IGN's preview from earlier this year. You can also check out the recent leak that spilled the full track list for the game's official album , and why we're excited to jump into Vice City, even if it's at 30 fps .
items.title_en: GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Will Start as Small-Time Criminals Who Have to Work Up to High-Value Jobs

items.title: EA Adds 'Don't Delete' Message to Madden NFL 27 in Bid to Keep Players From Making Room Ahead of GTA 6
items.excerpt: EA has added a "don't delete" pop-up message to Madden NFL 27, and players can't help but feel the company is begging them not to make room for Grand Theft Auto 6.
items.content_text: EA has added a "don't delete" pop-up message to Madden NFL 27 , and players can't help but feel the company is begging them not to make room for Grand Theft Auto 6 . Reports of the new in-game notice began cropping up over the weekend, with CharlieIntel relaying their findings online. EA doesn't explicitly mention GTA 6 in the new message, but considering the pop-up features some familiar pink-and-purple colors and sun-kissed palm trees, it's pretty easy to put two and two together. The message encourages Madden NFL 27 users to refrain from uninstalling the game from their devices, promising that those who stick around can look forward to a new update coming Tuesday, November 17. It's a bit beside the point, but we should also mention that, at least based on early screenshots, EA's message includes a typo, writing "awating signal" instead of "awaiting signal." Newer posts suggest it was fixed pretty quickly. Whoops! EA has added a 'Don't Delete!' message to EA Madden NFL 27 ahead of Grand Theft Auto VI's launch The in-game ad says there's an update on Nov 17 for the title, before GTA VI https://t.co/P00NPUVveK — CharlieIntel (@charlieINTEL) November 14, 2026 "Don't Delete!" the Madden pop-up says. "[ENCRYPTED SIGNAL] The target is locked. The crew is assembling for a high-stakes run. Await the signal from our insider on 11/17… do not leak this transmission!" There's just no getting around it; the next week is going to be very, very weird for the gaming industry. GTA 6, a decade-in-the-making video game said to bring the biggest launch of all time , has mostly seen every other game clear the calendar just to make room for it. The atmosphere surrounding Rockstar Games' latest is something to behold, and with millions of players still turning up for live-service titles, one can wonder if any of their developers are worried about GTA 6 taking a chunk of their attention. That at least seems to be the case for EA and Madden NFL 27. If a Vice City-themed pop-up in this year's annual football game release wasn't enough to convince you, its official X/Twitter account actually recently doubled down. A November 10 post promoting a November 18 update referenced GTA 6's massive file size by saying, "Don't let 210GB get between you and Your League." It all seems in good fun, but fans say they can't help but feel like EA is doing everything in its power to keep players interested. Some even say it feels like the company is begging them to stay. When one Reddit user asked what the message was related to, one user replied , "It means that EA is terrified of GTA VI's launch." Another said it felt like the pop-up was the publisher's way of saying, "'PLEASE DON'T DELETE MADDEN TO CLEAR SPACE FOR GTA. PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE!'" "EA begging us not to delete Madden is so funny," one X user said . "Respectfully I might never play your game again after GTA comes out," another added . @EAMaddenNFL Mf thinks we’re gonna be on Madden 😭✌️ https://t.co/q4YY8i7IGw — Austin 🦆 (@deviousduck_) November 11, 2026 @EAMaddenNFL Just deleted madden to create more space for my GTA6 https://t.co/qLUsaG9604 — Black (@blxckxbt) November 12, 2026 Madden NFL 27 launched for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S August 13, 2026. GTA 6 launches for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19, this week . For more on Rockstar's new game, you can read about the official album's leaked track list . For more on Madden, you can read about the open-world football game EA is cooking up behind the scenes .

items.title: Xbox at 25: My Memories From Across Xbox’s Entire (and Quite Incredible) History
items.excerpt: I’ve been lucky enough to have a front-row seat for most of the Xbox’s 25 years, covering the high highs and low lows of Microsoft’s pivot into the living room. It’s been quite a ride since November 15, 2001, and I wanted to mark the occasion by sharing some of my biggest memories with you. And, like everything else with Xbox, it started with Halo.
items.content_text: The first day of my career was October 1, 2002. I’d been lucky enough to get hired by Official Xbox Magazine. The fledgling Xbox console was not quite a year old, and when I got settled in on the staff, it quickly became clear that Xbox was really about one thing above all else: Halo. I remember being surprised in my first days on the job by what would happen every single day, like clockwork, at 5pm: consoles and TVs would get turned on, Halo would get fired up, and we’d all play a round or two of Capture the Flag on Blood Gulch before we all went home. Fun and friendly banter ensued. Halo was baked into the Xbox’s DNA from the very start. It is one of my very first of many thousands of great Xbox memories. I’ve been lucky enough to have a front-row seat for most of the Xbox’s 25 years, covering the high highs and low lows of Microsoft’s pivot into the living room. It’s been quite a ride since November 15, 2001, and I wanted to mark the occasion by sharing some of my biggest memories with you. And, like everything else with Xbox, it started with Halo. Thank goodness for Combat Evolved, in fact, because most of the rest of that first year of Xbox history was pretty bleak. Lots of C++ spaghetti was thrown at the wall, and most of it didn’t stick. Oh, don’t get me wrong – there were moments! Steel Battalion, Capcom’s batshit-insane mech vertical tank simulator that cost $200 and came with its own custom 40-button controller and foot pedals was quite simply amazing as both a game and piece of hardware and would never get made today. Meanwhile, The Elder Scrolls 3: Morrowind was the beginning of Xbox becoming a Western-RPG powerhouse. But first-party hadn’t really found its footing yet, as it published stuff like the now-infamous Blinx: The Time Sweeper. But thanks to Combat Evolved carrying the Xbox through its first trip around the sun, things got really interesting in Year Two. It turns out I joined the magazine at just the right time! Halo: Combat Evolved was the biggest very real reason to buy the console in its first year, but its critical second year was defined by three things: Xbox Live, Tom Clancy games, and BioWare. Year Two Xbox Live was a massive swing that connected for a home run. Back then, high-speed internet was far from ubiquitous. In fact, dial-up 56k modems still dominated the American online infrastructure. But Microsoft put a big bet on broadband by putting an Ethernet port into every Xbox. In the first year, that port only got used for Halo LAN (er, System Link) parties, but then, on the one-year anniversary of the system on November 15, 2002, Xbox Live launched. And it was a loud launch in the very best of ways. MechAssault brought an action-first take on MechWarrior to the console audience – including an excellent multiplayer suite – while a faithful port of the PC’s outstanding military FPS Tom Clancy’s Ghost Recon was a perfect fit for the new online service. And all of it was buttery smooth and almost entirely free of latency on account of everyone being on a high-speed connection. Plus, every Xbox Live kit came with a chat headset, and in those earliest days, people actually used them! Party Chat didn’t exist yet, so everyone talked to each other, and trolls were few and far between on account of the service having a $50 per year buy-in. A mere two days later, a second, wholly original (albeit single-player-only) Tom Clancy release dropped exclusively on Xbox: Splinter Cell. PlayStation had Solid Snake, but the young Xbox had the sardonic and effortlessly cool Sam Fisher (voiced to perfection by the irreplaceable Michael Ironside). Incredible real-time lighting, super-fun spy gadgets, memorable setpieces, and stellar stealth gameplay all combined to create an instant hit for Xbox – and one that also served as a technical showpiece for the console’s potent graphical capabilities. The Tom Clancy brand becoming synonymous with Xbox would only continue in 2003. The Tom Clancy brand becoming synonymous with Xbox would only continue in 2003, when yet another Tom Clancy gem, Rainbow Six 3, hit Xbox that holiday and did some truly awesome stuff. For one, it looked and sounded great. That was a common thread running through all of the early Clancy games on Xbox: great visuals and sublime Dolby 5.1 surround sound. But more than that, its campaign was augmented by a compelling new feature: commanding your AI squadmates with your voice. Remember that chat headset that was bundled in with every Xbox Live Starter Kit a year earlier? The brilliant designers at Ubisoft Montreal had put it to good use, allowing you to shout things like, “Go! Go! Go!” when all of your guys were stacked up at a door and ready to breach. I sounded like an absolute lunatic doing this in the middle of the OXM office as I reviewed the game, but did it add to the fun? Unequivocally, yes. And then that same chat headset got put to great use for its original purpose: online multiplayer. Rainbow Six 3 dominated Xbox Live; it was arguably the online service’s first killer app. Xbox Live programming director Larry “Major Nelson” Hryb used to regularly post the top 10 most-played games on Xbox Live, and Rainbow Six was firmly entrenched in the top spot for months after its release (until November of 2004; you can probably guess why, but we’ll get to that…). But 2003 saw far more than just one significant release for Xbox. That summer gave us one of the five best original Xbox games ever – a truly special release that doubled as one of the best Star Wars games ever made and tripled as one of the best RPGs ever made. And I had the tremendous pleasure of reviewing it. It was, of course, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, an epic tale set thousands of years before the original film trilogy that let you fully embrace either the Light Side or Dark Side of the Force. I opted for the latter, mostly because no game I’d ever played had fully supported evil choices. But KOTOR absolutely did, allowing me to double-cross people I’d made deals with and generally just be terrible. It was glorious, and it legitimized RPGs on the Xbox . I still remember driving 45 minutes from the OXM office to Skywalker Ranch to get the review build installed on my Xbox debug kit. I had no idea what a ride I was about to go on, and to this day KOTOR remains either my 1a or 1b favorite RPG of all time, along with the very next Xbox-exclusive game the KOTOR development team at BioWare would make, which I’ll talk more about later. Grand Theft Auto 3 and Vice City also came to Xbox in 2003 as part of the GTA Double Pack, as did Max Payne 2 and one of Xbox Live’s first big multiplayer hits, the class-based first-person shooter Return to Castle Wolfenstein: Tides of War. The much-hyped first-party exclusive Brute Force dropped that year, too, and though it couldn’t quite live up to its “The Next Halo?” headline we’d put on it on the cover of OXM ahead of its release, it was nevertheless pretty good, though it failed to take off. But Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge, a console continuation of a previous PC game, very much did, becoming another Xbox Live hit. So did the golf action of Links 2004 and the tennis competition found in Top Spin – two pillars of the short-lived XSN program. Voodoo Vince, meanwhile, was a really good platformer even if it didn’t sell all that well. But you know what did? Project Gotham Racing 2, a semi-realistic racer that deftly straddled the line between sim and arcade and proved to be a huge success. First party was finally starting to find its footing beyond Halo. Halo Freakin’ 2 Xbox’s third year built on the impressive momentum of the previous one. A murderer’s row of killer games hit the console in 2004. You already know the big one, but let’s not forget about the rest. In fact, the 2004 lineup begins with another top-five original-Xbox GOAT, Ninja Gaiden. Designer Tomonobu Itagaki (may he rest in peace ) and Team Ninja followed its Dead or Alive 3 day-one Xbox launch title with a revival of the 1980’s arcade and NES classic, translated gloriously into a 3D fast-action challenge of your wits and skill. My colleague Mitchell Saltzman, a connoisseur of the genre, called Ninja Gaiden the best pure action game ever made – and he did so 20 years after Ninja Gaiden’s release. And he’s absolutely right . We had a playable demo of Ninja Gaiden on the OXM demo disc prior to its release, and we got enthusiastic letters about it for months on end. That demo probably sold tens of thousands of copies of that game, and it was a point of pride and a privilege for us to be able to be the vehicle for introducing so many Xbox gamers to it. Just a few weeks later, Splinter Cell returned with Pandora Tomorrow, delivering another excellent stealth campaign. But that’s not what Splinter Cell’s first sequel is best remembered for. That honor goes to another reason you absolutely had to pony up the $50 annual subscription for Xbox Live if you hadn’t already: the wholly original, wildly innovative Spies vs. Mercenaries multiplayer mode. In it, two Sam Fisher-like Spies – playing from the same third-person perspective as the single-player campaign – faced off against two first-person-viewing, heavily armed Mercs as they battled over objectives. Spies were nonlethal with one notable exception: if they could sneak up behind the Merc and grab him around the neck from behind, not only could they break said neck to take them out, but the mic chat would suddenly open up, allowing the Spy to vocally taunt the Merc before making the kill. It was genius stuff that’s still revered today. I’ve already written extensively about The Chronicles of Riddick: Escape from Butcher Bay and shared my memories of when developer Starbreeze first brought it to the OXM office, but hoo-boy, what a masterpiece this was. All of a sudden, licensed games weren’t terrible by default. I’d go so far as to say a lot of games based on an existing IP owe a debt of gratitude to Riddick. Which brings me to Fable. Is it on the short list of best Xbox games ever? Admittedly, not quite – and I say that as the person who reviewed it for OXM and gave it a very strong 8.9 out of 10. But it did successfully birth a franchise, and it was a great game. It had the unfortunate burden of having to live up to series co-creator Peter Molyneux’s boasts and promises – most notably how Fable would have such advanced systems that you could plant an acorn early in the game, and by the end of the campaign it would grow into a full tree (you couldn’t). But this was a world full of charm and humor and some really high-quality action-adventuring. And it was a hit! And then there was Halo 2. Where to even begin? It was probably the most fun I’ve ever had in my career covering a single game. The buildup to November 9, 2004 was unlike anything I’ve experienced as a gamer or as a media professional both before and since. The hype was truly unprecedented – everyone was fired up for it. In the pre-social media era where monoculture was still alive, Halo 2 had everyone’s attention. I’ve never been more excited for a first hands-on with a game than I was the first time I laid hands on Halo 2 back at E3 2004. The year prior, Bungie showed the now-infamous single-player demo – but nobody in the media got to play it. In 2004, however, my first taste of Halo 2 came from a single-flag CTF match on the Zanzibar map during E3. Dual-wielding weapons, boarding vehicles, the new graphics, the new weapons – it was all in there! Remember, we’d been playing Halo 1 multiplayer at OXM every day ; we’d never stopped. So to say I was excited for the first new Halo of any kind since the original would be a colossal understatement. These behind-closed-doors multiplayer sessions were by appointment only, and as you can imagine, they were booked solid throughout the entire week of E3. But inevitably there were no-shows here and there, and I was able to sneak my way back in for a couple more rounds that week. Afterwards, all I could think about was Halo 2. Luckily for me, Bungie held an all-day multiplayer hands-on session at its studio later that summer, and somehow none of my more senior OXM colleagues pulled rank, so I got to go. I was like a kid set loose in the Wonka chocolate factory as I took in as many maps and modes as I could (which wasn’t all of them, as Bungie intended to keep some secret for launch, but more on that shortly). You literally had to cut the magazine spread open if you wanted to see the surprise reveal of Coagulation. And then, as Halo 2’s November 9 release started getting closer, we got the call from Bungie: we’d been invited up to do a world-exclusive review of Halo 2 for an OXM cover story. Because magazine lead times are quite long – meaning, it has to be done quite far in advance to hit the magazine’s newsstand on-sale date – it meant that I found myself at Bungie at the end of September in 2004 with our editor-in-chief, Rob Smith. I wrote all about this recently , but one thing I didn’t mention in that piece was the secret map thing. Through our multiple days of time with both the campaign and the multiplayer, we discovered that Bungie was hiding a surprise for Halo fans: a remake of one of Combat Evolved’s most beloved multiplayer maps, Blood Gulch. It was called Coagulation in Halo 2, but Bungie didn’t want us to spoil the surprise. Rob and I argued that we’re reviewing the game and thus it was fair game for the magazine because it was part of what we wanted to talk about. The compromise we reached was to do a special sealed page in the OXM review. You literally had to cut the magazine spread open if you wanted to see the surprise reveal of Coagulation. By the way, that wasn’t an easy thing to arrange with our magazine printer! It was the one and only time we ever did it. The Road to Next-Gen I’m going year-by-year here because the first handful of years for Xbox were both important and extremely memorable. I promise I’m not going to write about every single one of the Xbox’s 25 years, but I certainly have to talk about 2005, as it was a pivotal year for the upstart American console brand. Everyone remembers 2005 as the launch of Xbox’s most successful console, the Xbox 360, but that wasn’t until November. The original Xbox went out with a heck of a bang in the 10 months leading up to that. In March, Ubisoft Montreal dropped another banger in the form of Splinter Cell Chaos Theory. It was three masterpiece games in one – another Michael Ironside-voiced stealth sandbox campaign, an evolved Spies vs. Mercenaries mode that added an extra player on each side for 3v3 matches, and a pioneering two-players-required four-mission co-op campaign (later upped to six via two free DLC missions) that ended up serving as a sneak preview for the It Takes Twos and Split Fictions we enjoy today. I gave it a 9.9 out of 10 – OXM’s highest score ever at the time (Halo: Combat Evolved got a 9.6 and our aforementioned boss Rob Smith gave Halo 2 a 9.7) – and it’s a score I still firmly believe in today. Chaos Theory already flexed the Xbox’s graphical muscles, but in April, id Software dropped a stunning Xbox-console-exclusive port of Doom 3, which was top-shelf PC stuff when it was released just eight months prior. BioWare followed up KOTOR with another Xbox exclusive: Jade Empire, which IGN gave a 9.9 out of 10 to at the time. Psychonauts hit that same month, debuting on Xbox first and bringing another game-design legend, Tim Schafer, into the Xbox fold for the first – but not last – time. Forza Motorsport was the start of something truly special in May, while Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas finally came to Xbox in June. The fur-shaded Conker: Live and Reloaded was Rare’s first proper Xbox project after Microsoft bought the revered studio from Nintendo in 2002. And just before we said hello to the Xbox 360, Valve brought the brilliant Half-Life 2 to a console for the first time with a port to the original Xbox in November. The Next Xbox Word of the next-gen Xbox – codename: Project Xenon – built throughout 2005. At OXM, we had the great privilege of getting all of the information on the new console well in advance on account of those aforementioned magazine lead times. Because of this, Microsoft required that our open-office space within the bullpen of our publisher, Future, be walled in and secured with a locked door. Nobody outside of the eight of us on the OXM staff could see what was on our screens and, later, on our desks. At E3 2005, I happened to have an Exhibitor badge, because our company, Future, had a booth on the show floor. That meant I could access the halls of the Los Angeles Convention Center before E3 properly opened. I remember being on my way to Future’s booth but passing by 2K’s floor space and spotting a Top Spin 2 kiosk. It was powered up and ready to play, so I picked up the controller – my first time picking up the revised Xbox 360 “Krypton” controller (as it was so codenamed), which became the template for many gamepads that would follow it, from Xbox’s own revisions to Nintendo’s Pro Controller to even the PS5’s DualSense, to a degree. This all-too-brief (and unauthorized) hands-on was technically my first time actually playing an Xbox 360 game, though it was on the initial development kit, which was – fun fact – a PowerMac G5! Later that year – after a preview cover story I wrote for OXM that summer that sent me to Infinity Ward to get the first hands-on with the day-one Xbox 360 title, Call of Duty 2 – I had the excitement of going to pick up our Xbox 360 debug consoles in September (when I say debug kit, it means that it was an Xbox capable of playing unfinished builds of a game, whereas a regular retail Xbox can only play games that have been certified by Microsoft). I don’t think I’d ever been more excited to get my hands on a new console. Sadly, we didn’t have much to play on them at first – we played a lot of the built-in puzzler Hexic HD, and I recall getting Amped 3 quite early – but even poking around the new (and retroactively beloved) Blades Dashboard interface was endlessly entertaining. When November 22, 2005 finally came and the Xbox 360 was released – just four short years after the launch of the original Xbox – it would prove to be the peak of Xbox’s popularity and public perception. Yes, the Red Ring of Death scandal was a serious problem in the following year or two, but the Xbox 360 was so popular and well-loved that somehow the brand made it through relatively unscathed. It started with an excellent day-one launch lineup that, while lacking any Halo-caliber killers, nevertheless brought 18 games to the table, including Call of Duty 2 (thus marking the beginning of CoD’s ascent to the top of the mainstream ), Project Gotham Racing 3, Perfect Dark Zero and Kameo from Rare, and the underrated horror game Condemned: Criminal Origins. Glory Days 2006 and 2007 were unquestionably the glory days of the Xbox 360 and, by extension, of Xbox. We knew we had it good back then; we just didn’t know that, even though we’ve had plenty of amazing games since, it would never reach those high highs again. Between first-party and third-party, Xbox was on a generational run in the 360’s first two full calendar years. Following that very good day-one launch lineup in November 2005, Xbox 360 kicked off its 2006 with the face-melting graphics of Fight Night Round 3, aka the first “holy sh*t!” graphics moment of the newly launched HD Era, in February. The next month, we got the next-gen-exclusive – and thus, Xbox 360-exclusive for the time, in the absence of the PlayStation 3 – Ghost Recon Advanced Warfighter (GRAW), immediately followed by what was, in my humble opinion, the 360’s first true killer app: The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion. You simply had to play this game. It was that stunning of an open-world, and a true step change from what we saw on the original Xbox and The Elder Scrolls 3: Morrowind. Some of my fo…

items.excerpt: The full track list for Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album seems to have leaked online just days before GTA 6's launch.
items.content_text: The full track list for Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album seems to have leaked online just days before GTA 6 's launch. Rockstar Games just can't catch a break. After weeks of unprecedented leaks were published online, even more information about GTA 6 has found its way onto the internet, this time revealing the entire list of every song and artist featured on the official soundtrack's album release. As 13 years turns into just a few days, more leaks felt inevitable. The latest breach arrived in the form of a video shared on social media from what appears to be a Barnes & Noble-like retailer. The main clip being passed around is still up hours later and shows the front, back, and spines of the Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album's double LP vinyl. As you might have guessed, the $50 soundtrack isn't planned to hit store shelves until November 19, 2026. Although there are likely even more tunes tucked into the game itself, an early glimpse at the GTA 6 soundtrack means we now know every song and artist featured on its official album. Rolling Stone has confirmed the track list with its sources. We won't beat around the bush; you can see the full Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album track list below. Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album Leaked Track List Side A Starting from Zero – Justice (feat. Michael McDonald) That's It – Yung Lean (feat. Future & Metro Boomin) Ahh Yea – Playboi Carti Rhyno – Travis Scott Sexy Magic – CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, PinkPantheress, Fred Again.. & Étienne de Crécy Flower in a Hurricane – Justice (feat. Tame Impala, SZA & King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard) Go Easy – Dua Lipa Last Thing You Need – Morgan Wallen Side B X – Jhayco Suzuki – Fuerza Regida Macacoa 2000 – Rauw Alejandro Dance With Me – Boogie Wit Da Hoodie (feat. Elkan) Bigger – Burna Boy Count Up – Gunna Let's Rock – Kodak Black & Don Toliver Wakin Up Flex – Young Thug IKYFL – Tee Grizzly TF? – Don Toliver Side C Don't Chart – Cardi B GMA – JT Power Trip – Jennie Blood in Your Eyes – Tove Lo Fast Emotion – Zara Larsson Sweet Like Candy – Camila Cabello Only One – Fcukers Sanduneguea – Arca TRDWFE – Rina Sawayama Side D All Again – Rose Gray Crazy for You – Lana Del Rey Largate – Kali Uchis & Helado Negro No Me Busques – Omar Apollo Bright Lights, Big City – Keith Richards Stone Cold Krazy Luuv – Jesse Johnson & DāM-FunK Overtown Lights – Stanley Clarke, Yussef Dayes & Robert Glasper We've gotten tastes of the music Rockstar hand-selected to be featured through the years, with stars like Travis Scott, Future, and Morgan Wallen teasing their inclusion as recently as September . We also got to hear some of GTA 6's tunes with the premiere of the Extended Look back in August. As many guessed, the developers have given players a solid playlist of songs from a variety of genres to jam to as they speed through Vice City. Fans will note this is different from the Grand Theft Auto VI: Original Score by Grammy Award-winning French electronic duo Justice. It's also set to get its own release for physical music collectors, with its release date set for December 11, 2026. GTA 6, of course, will launch for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X | S November 19, 2026. Today, we also learned that Rockstar has promised next week's new game will include mechanisms to encourage empathy for the first time in the franchise's history . Yesterday, Rockstar revealed a closer look at an animated TV series called Macca & Friends that can be watched in-game. items.title: League of Legends: New Dawn Unveiled With Debut Trailer, Riot Announces Major Overhaul Coming in 2027
items.excerpt: At the 2026 League of Legends World Championship Finals, Riot Games officially unveiled League of Legends: New Dawn. The large-scale update is scheduled for 2027 and will bring changes to the game's client, Summoner's Rift, visuals, and gameplay, marking the beginning of a new chapter for one of the industry's most enduring titles.
items.content_text: At the 2026 League of Legends World Championship Finals, Riot Games officially unveiled League of Legends: New Dawn. The large-scale update is scheduled for 2027 and will bring changes to the game's client, Summoner's Rift, visuals, and gameplay, marking the beginning of a new chapter for one of the industry's most enduring titles. New Dawn introduces what Riot described as an "all-encompassing" update to League, touching almost every aspect of its experience. "This is the start of a new era for League, a new journey," said Paul Bellezza, League's executive producer, in New Dawn's first official trailer. Riot is expected to share the full reveal of New Dawn this coming January. A new look for Summoner's Rift The announcement came with a trailer shown at Worlds Finals that offered the first glimpse of what League players can expect from New Dawn, and the changes appear to go beyond simple refreshed graphics. The first noticeable change is a redesigned champion selection screen, which looks much closer to the modern interface found in Wild Rift, League's mobile game. The footage also hints at a new or reworked rune system, which seems to have a much bigger impact on the gameplay than ever before. The trailer also showcased updated minions, a new look for Summoner's Rift, redesigned dragons and Baron Nashor, as well as what seem to be new visual effects for many champion abilities. More interestingly, the footage also hinted at gameplay changes that will change how players approach their matches, including major changes to the map terrain that open new strategic consideration — and not only for junglers. Since its launch in 2009, League has seen more than a few major changes, including a rebuilt Summoner's Rift in 2014, a new client a couple of years later, and runes and then terrain changes in the following years. Still, nothing ever came close to the scale of what New Dawn promises to be. For now, Riot is keeping the full extent of these gameplay changes to itself, leaving much of New Dawn's scope to be revealed in the coming months. Leaving the past behind Riot spent part of 2026 looking back at League's history through League Classic, a mode that allowed players to revisit older versions of both the Summoner's Rift and League's champions. However, nostalgia alone proved difficult to sustain. Just a few weeks after its release, Riot announced that the mode would end its current run in January 2027. The experience could return in a modified format in the future, but it demonstrated that revisiting the past is not necessarily enough to keep a game of League's scale moving forward. Now, Riot is looking in the opposite direction. 18 years since League first launched, New Dawn represents another attempt at evolving a game whose identity has been shaped as much by its community as by its developers. But whether players embrace the changes or push back against them remains to be seen. After all, it is the playerbase that will ultimately decide whether this new chapter gives League the foundation it needs to thrive for another decade or sends it down a different path. More information about League of Legends: New Dawn is expected in the coming weeks, with Riot's full presentation scheduled for some time in January 2027.

items.title: Resident Evil Requiem Star Hopes Grace Ashcroft Has 'a Long Way to Go' Even if She Won't 'Ever Be a Leon Character'
items.excerpt: Grace Ashcroft actress Angela Sant'Albano doesn't think her Resident Evil Requiem hero will "ever be a Leon character," but she's still hoping "there's a long way to go with her."
items.content_text: Grace Ashcroft actress Angela Sant'Albano doesn't think her Resident Evil Requiem hero will "ever be a Leon character," but she's still hoping "there's a long way to go with her." The person behind one of 2026's standout video game roles laid out her hopes for the future during an interview with GamesRadar . Resident Evil Requiem may only be a few months old, but she's already got a good idea of how she'd like to see Grace grow should she be asked to brave manmade horrors beyond comprehension yet again. Warning! Spoilers for Resident Evil Requiem follow. "I would really love to see how her relationship with Leon blossoms," Sant'Albano explained. "I think we have a beautiful mentorship, almost brotherly, sisterly relationship brewing. And I also want to know what happens with her and Emily." Assuming you chose the 'good' ending, Resident Evil Requiem closes with the series' one-liner expert, Leon S. Kennedy, alive and Grace taking Emily under her wing. It painted a bright future for the crew, and although it almost certainly won't last, it did give the developers at Capcom plenty of room to grow new and old characters alike. Despite some pretty deep roots in Resident Evil lore, Grace's story in the franchise is really only getting started in Resident Evil Requiem. So far, there's been no word on whether she'll stick around for additional entries and eventually stand toe-to-toe with other protagonists like Ethan Winters or Chris Redfield. Judging by the strong impression she made when her debut game launched in February, we wouldn't be surprised to see her back at some point down the line. Sant'Albano knows Grace could survive another run in with mutated monsters after making it through the horrors of the Rhodes Hill Chronic Care Center, but will she ever be dodging chainsaws with carefully timed but stylish backflips? Not likely. "I don't think she'll ever be a Leon character," Sant'Albano said. "She's never going to be badass, you know, doing roundhouse kicks. But I do think her courage and her self-esteem will grow the more that she trusts herself and forgives herself for a lot of the things that I think tie her down. So, I think there's a long way to go with her." Resident Evil Requiem is still so fresh, so we probably won't hear about another mainline entry like a potential Resident Evil 10 anytime soon . As if there was any doubt, that doesn't mean Capcom plans to keep players waiting for more. In 2027, fans will step back into the shoes of Resident Evil 2 hero Claire Redfield for Resident Evil Veronica . It's been a while since we last heard an update on that front following its announcement in June. We're also still waiting to hear more about the story DLC the publisher promised back in March. Maybe we could see more Grace there? IGN gave Resident Evil Requiem a 9/10 review . At the time of its launch, we said it "successfully splices two separate strains of survival horror together into one highly infectious new mutation."

items.title: 'It Felt Criminal' — Adam Driver Still Can't Believe How Disney Handled Canceled Star Wars Movie The Hunt for Ben Solo
items.excerpt: Adam Driver still can't believe Disney killed his Star Wars movie, The Hunt for Ben Solo, and has now gone so far as to say that the move "felt criminal."
items.content_text: Adam Driver still can't believe Disney killed his Star Wars movie, The Hunt for Ben Solo, and has now gone so far as to say that the move "felt criminal." The Kylo Ren/Ben Solo actor relived some of the darker parts of his past with the massive sci-fi franchise during a recent conversation with AP . His updated thoughts on the matter follow years of work and months of fan organizing, and although he and director Steven Soderbergh have almost nothing to show for it, he's still pretty fired up about how it all went down. "For me it was: Steven Soderbergh wants to make a Star Wars film," Driver said. "What are we debating? It’s what it is. It’s criminal. Or it felt criminal. We’re all moving on. On to the next. And Steven already has something else that’s one of the best things he’s ever written." We first learned about The Hunt for Ben Solo, a Skywalker Saga follow-up that explored a potential future for its title character, when Driver called it one of the "coolest scripts" he had "ever been a part of" late last year. Despite the hype, it never came to be, mostly because, according to Driver, then-Disney CEO Bob Iger and co-chairman Alan Bergman "didn't see how Ben Solo was alive." What followed was months of additional words from those who worked on the shuttered project, including Soderbergh, who called Disney's decision to pull the plug after two-and-a-half years of work "insane." Before long, fans orchestrated their own campaign to try and save the movie , but at least as far as August 2026, Lucasfilm president Dave Filoni has said that it's not something the company is working on right now . With so much work put into it, it's been hard for many to see why Disney would shut down an impassioned pitch from a fan-favorite Star Wars actor. Driver himself still seems confused about the call to this day. The silver lining, though, was how dedicated fans chipped in to see his and Soderbergh's ideas brought to life. "I was blown away by the response to it," Driver added. "In no way did I think there would be billboards in Times Square. It’s so moving. It did feel like we were all at the bar having a conversation about the films we wanted to see." For now, however, Driver is most likely hanging up his hilted lightsaber for good. He said as much during another interview earlier this month, though he's still leaving the door open should Disney change its mind about The Hunt for Ben Solo . Soderbergh, who is currently helping out with The Batman Part 2 , ruled out a return in April of this year. Taika Waititi's long-gestating Star Wars movie joined the Ben Solo film when it was officially put on ice last month . While Star Wars' future has plenty of question marks to address , there are a few projects confirmed to launch in the next year alone. You can see IGN's full breakdown for every movie and show in development here .

items.title: Chris Pratt Says He 'Would Love' James Gunn to Return for Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 4 After Leaving DC
items.excerpt: Chris Pratt said he would love to reunite with James Gunn for Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 4 after the director abruptly announced he would be leaving DC Studios earlier this week.
items.content_text: Chris Pratt said he would love to reunite with James Gunn for Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 4 after the director abruptly announced he would be leaving DC Studios earlier this week. Gunn is no longer running DC movies with Peter Safran – so what comes next? That's the question many comic book fans are asking as the dust begins to settle at Skydance, and although it will be quite a while before we actually see what happens, some are getting their hopes up for a Marvel reunion. Gunn directed three Guardians of the Galaxy movies for the Marvel Cinematic Universe (and dealt with his fair share of drama ) while working with the Marvel Studios team before leaving to help head up DC Studios in 2022 . Work on Man of Tomorrow and one other mystery DC project aside , the comic book movie maker's future is wide open. Chris Pratt, who has starred as the MCU's Star-Lord for more than a decade, told Moviezine it would be "awesome" to re-team with Gunn for Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 4 now that DC is about nearly in the rearview mirror. "That would be awesome. I love working with James. He's the man," Pratt said. "I haven't had a chance to speak with him since that news came out yesterday." The last time we saw Star-Lord and the rest of the Guardians was in 2023's Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 . Although that story fit well as a bookend for its characters and Gunn's work on the franchise, fans have had a hard time letting go of some of the MCU's most popular faces – Pratt included. In January of this year, the actor said he has a "really strong vision" to bring Star-Lord back in future MCU installments. Just last month, he promised that plans for his return were in the works at Marvel Studios . Gamora actor Zoe Saldaña also said in 2024 that "it would be a huge loss" if the space-traveling heroes were left behind . Gunn coming back to Marvel again feels like a long shot, and it's always possible that we could see the Guardians return in another MCU ensemble film like next year's Avengers: Secret Wars . At least for now, Pratt is willing to hold out hope. "All I'll say is, I love James," he added. "He directed all three [Guardians of the Galaxy movies], and that's pretty rare in those types of trilogies, to have the same director through all three. If he wanted to come back and bring it back, man. I would love that." Whether it's with the MCU or DC, much of the future is a mystery. In Gunn's case, we at least know Skydance has yet to even see his cut of Man of Tomorrow after the director squashed rumors claiming otherwise last night. We'll know about what's coming down the pipe for Marvel when Avengers: Doomsday arrives next month.
